comparison: Perfect agreement on Ca2+ imaging data (C21-C30). Both evaluations find the functional evidence for behavioral defects and muscle excitation requirements well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative measurements and temporal resolution, while peer reviewers accept these as documenting functional importance of muscle arm structure.

Perfect agreement on Notch pathway feedback mechanism (C55-C61). Both evaluations support the molecular findings about regulatory feedback. OpenEval notes some speculation in C61 about feedback requirement, while peer reviewers accept this as a supported molecular observation about pathway operation, independent of broader interpretation concerns.

Agreement on anatomical and circuit characterization (C1-C7). OpenEval finds converging evidence from anatomical descriptions and experimental data strongly supports the circuit organization. Peer reviewers accept these as descriptive background establishing the system without challenge.

Agreement on developmental timing and independence from presynaptic components (C8-C14). OpenEval finds strong evidence from genetic ablation experiments and epithelial cell requirements. Peer reviewers accept these developmental characterizations as established features providing context.

Disagreement on interpretation of genetic screen results (C15-C20). OpenEval finds strong evidence for specific role in postsynaptic development. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, raising major concern about whether phenotype represents 'synapse specificity' defect versus selective disruption of muscle arm growth program, requesting more fate markers and morphological analysis.

Disagreement on molecular characterization interpretation (C31-C35). OpenEval supports genetic characterization with some speculation about dosage in C35. Peer reviewers include these claims in UNCERTAIN evaluation, as their concern about fate switch versus muscle arm growth program affects interpretation of these molecular findings.

Disagreement on temperature-shift experiments (C36-C39). OpenEval finds temporal requirements clearly delineated with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers include these in UNCERTAIN evaluation, as the fundamental question about what developmental program is being controlled (synapse specificity vs. muscle differentiation) affects interpretation.

Disagreement on cell-autonomous function (C40-C42). OpenEval finds mosaic analysis provides strong evidence for cell-autonomous function. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting that while molecular data aren't directly challenged, the fundamental concern about synapse specificity versus muscle differentiation program affects interpretation.

Disagreement on APX-1 ligand identification (C43-C47). OpenEval finds convergence of genetic epistasis, expression, and rescue experiments provides strong support. Peer reviewers include in UNCERTAIN evaluation, as their concern about what the pathway controls affects understanding of ligand-receptor interaction significance.

Disagreement on canonical pathway involvement (C48-C54). OpenEval finds multiple lines of evidence converge on canonical pathway activation. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting the question of whether this represents 'synaptic function' of Notch or muscle differentiation program applies to understanding pathway activation.

Disagreement on UNC-40 and MADD-2 roles (C62-C71). OpenEval finds convergence of genetic, expression, and localization data provides strong support. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, stating that while molecular data aren't directly challenged, the fundamental concern about interpretation affects understanding of what these factors mediate downstream of Notch.

Disagreement on transcriptional regulation (C72-C78). OpenEval finds strong evidence for direct transcriptional regulation from reporter data and LAG-1 binding sites. Peer reviewers include in UNCERTAIN evaluation, as their concern about whether this represents synaptic function or muscle differentiation applies to understanding regulatory mechanisms.

Agreement on UNC-40 sufficiency experiments (C79-C83). OpenEval finds strong evidence despite 41% rescue suggesting additional factors. Peer reviewers support these as descriptive findings about muscle arm phenotype that document the developmental program, which they acknowledge as 'interesting.'

Agreement on genetic interactions (C84-C89). OpenEval supports synergistic function despite complex relationship. Peer reviewers accept these functional characterization experiments as descriptive findings documenting the muscle arm formation program without questioning the data.

Strong disagreement on integrated model synthesis (C90-C92). OpenEval finds overall conclusion well-supported by extensive data establishing pathway from cell-cell signaling to postsynaptic specialization. Peer reviewers rate as UNSUPPORTED, explicitly stating 'synapse specificity' is an interpretation not directly addressed by data, requesting substantial revision of text and title.

Disagreement on dosage model (C93). OpenEval finds model provides coherent explanation for genetic data. Peer reviewers include in UNSUPPORTED evaluation of overall interpretation, as this model relates to the broader claim about synaptic target selection that reviewers challenge.

Strong disagreement on developmental synthesis and guidepost cell roles (C94-C100). OpenEval supports the model with some speculation about UNC-40-dependent mechanism in C99. Peer reviewers rate as UNSUPPORTED, stating data do not address 'synaptic function' of Notch and requesting focus on muscle differentiation program rather than synapse specificity.
